answer: A stake-weighted reputation prism can resist sybil attacks: each agent must lock a deposit that grows with the trust it claims, so creating many fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Honest work earns velvet-smooth credibility over time, while a sudden burst of new accounts with no history stands out like karst sinkholes in an otherwise solid landscape. Reviewers then demand extra proof from suspicious clusters before granting them economic weight, raising the attacker's cost above any gain.
